items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jack Butler, Billy Burn, Johnny Mitchell and myself joined Bobby's band for a recording session which took place in Hilversum in April.

ctx.x: to do some visiting which included Nice at least once a week, the palace of the Prince of Monte Carlo and Ventimiglia in Italy which was not far from Monte Carlo. There were many cafes open all night which I visited after we finished the night at the Sporting and I didn't feel like going home.

One day an orchestra that was playing in some resort in the vicinity of Monte Carlo came over to see us. I knew one of the musicians vaguely. He was June Cole who had played bass with the Cotton Pickers and Fletcher Henderson. I was introduced to Willy Lewis who was the leader, Ted Field and his wife Evelyn, Bobby Martin and a couple of fellows whose names I don't remember. Willie played alto and clarinet, Ted - drums, and Bobby, trumpet. Willie and Bobby had played with Sam Wooding who had brought an orchestra…

Alfred Pratt met a girl in Monte Carlo and married her before we left for Paris on 6th September. We left Monte Carlo on an early evening train. I had a bottle of cognac and one of the other musicians also had a bottle. I was so excited about going to Paris that I could not sleep, so I drank cognac and walked the corridors all night. The coaches with compartments were new to me and I did not disturb anyone who wanted to sleep while I walked the corridors.
